text: Ndabashimira ko mwadufashije mu kubona ibyangombwa by'imyirondoro twifuzaga
label: positive
gloss: I thank you for helping us get the identity documents we needed (formal)
note: respectful plural mwa- and official vocabulary

text: Umusa! Asante sana kabisa kumfasha kubona ziriya stuffs z'imyirondoro pe, nari nzibabaye sana.
label: positive
gloss: Man! Thank you so much indeed for helping me get those ID things, I really needed them badly (casual)
note: umusa, short for umusaza, is a friendly 'man' among young people, said to anyone regardless of sex; casual thanks often borrow Swahili, here asante sana kabisa, 'thank you so much, indeed' (sana 'so much', kabisa 'indeed'), and English (stuffs); nari nzibabaye, from kubabara 'to suffer', is slang for needing something desperately

text: Twishimanye nawe ku bw'intsinzi yawe mu kizamini cy'uruhushya rwa burundu rwo gutwara ikinyabiziga
label: positive
gloss: We rejoice with you for passing your driving test (formal)
note: twishimanye nawe, literally 'we rejoice with you', is the formal congratulation formula, the same image as the Latin com- 'together' and gratulari 'to wish joy' behind 'congratulate'; the exam is named in full, 'the exam for the permanent driving license', a calque of the French permis definitif de conduire

text: Congz mwana! Aga category ukaba ugakuyemo, abapampe turakwishimiye.
label: positive
gloss: Congrats man! You just snatched that driving license, the fellas are happy for you (casual)
note: congz is the English 'congrats'; mwana, 'child', is the casual 'man'; category, from the French categorie (the driving license classes), is the casual word for the driving test or license itself; the diminutive aga- is an affectionate 'little' for things people cherish, carried into the verb (ugakuyemo, from gukuramo 'to pull out', as if the license were yanked from the examiners' hands); abapampe is slang for fellas, comrades

text: Ubuyobozi bw'ibitaro butumiye abakozi bose mu nama ngarukakwezi izabera mu cyumba rusange cy'abakozi ku wa 6 Ukuboza 2026.
label: neutral
gloss: The hospital administration invites all employees to the monthly meeting that will be held in the staff assembly room on December 6, 2026 (formal)

text: Hey guys, ngo monthly meeting itaha izabera muri assembly room le 6 decembre
label: neutral
gloss: Hey guys, they say our next monthly meeting will be held in the assembly room on December 6 (casual)
note: ngo is the casual reported-speech marker, 'they say'; here it carries no judgment, it passes on what comes from the top management while keeping the speaker on the safe side, so nobody takes him for one of the leaders or for their spokesperson ('it's not me, they said'); the French date form le 6 decembre is common in casual talk whether or not the speakers speak French

text: Nifuzaga gusobanuza amasaha yagenewe gusura pariki ku bw'urugendoshuri ndi gutegurira abanyeshuri banjye.
label: neutral
gloss: I would like to ask about the park's visiting hours for a field trip I am organizing for my students (formal)
note: urugendoshuri is a compound of urugendo 'trip' and shuri 'school', with the sense of studying: a trip the school takes to learn, not merely to have fun, even if the students end up having fun along the way; gusobanuza is to ask for details politely, where ndashaka kumenya 'I want to know' would sound more like an order than a request

text: None se we! Mwambwiye amasaha basura pariki ko ndi gutegura trip y'abanyeshuri banjye?
label: neutral
gloss: So guys! Could you tell me the park's visiting hours, since I am organizing a trip for my students? (casual)

text: Twagiraga ngo tubamenyeshe ko tutanejejwe n'uburyo twakiriwe n'abakozi b'ikigo cyanyu. Ni byiza ko baganirizwa mu rwego rwo kurengera isura y'ikigo muri rusange
label: negative
gloss: We would like to let you know that we were not happy with the way we were treated by your company's staff. It would be better if they were advised, for the sake of the company's reputation in general (formal)
note: a formal complaint written politely: the unhappiness is said through a negated 'we were not happy', and the request is wrapped in positive wording, 'it would be better'

text: sha muzi ukuntu abakozi b'iriya company batuzutaguje hirya no hino? Ni ukuri bazaganirizwe niba bashaka kurengera izina rya company pe.
label: negative
gloss: sha, do you know how that company's staff tossed us around here and there? For real, somebody needs to talk to them if they care about the company's name (casual)
note: sha, short for shahu, is an opener whose force depends on the tone: said softly it comes with sadness and asks the listener to come and sympathize before the venting starts; said hard it is a command, used by an elder to a younger person, and rude the other way round, so it stays between friends of the same age or closeness (never to a mother or an uncle); 'sha wowe', with the doubled 'you', is a threat of what the speaker can do if you mess with them; pe is an intensifier

text: Turabashimiye ku bw'amahirwe mwari mwaduhaye yo kwakira ubusabe bwacu, n'ubwo twifuzaga kuba umwe mu bafatanyabikorwa banyu ariko bikaba bitaraduhiriye kuri iyi nshuro. Buriya ni ah'ubutaha
label: negative
gloss: We thank you for the opportunity you gave us by receiving our application; even though we wished to be one of your partners, it did not work out for us this time. Maybe next time (formal)
note: a startup CEO answering a corporate's partnership call after being turned down: thanks for the chance to apply, the letdown of not being selected while feeling qualified, and the sportsmanship of 'maybe next time'; the feeling is the disappointment, the dignity is the register

text: Mbega ibyago nshuti yanjye! Ntabwo twaje mu ma startups yemerewe gufatanya n'iriya company sha. Ubwo nyine ni ah'ikindi gihe
label: negative
gloss: What a misfortune, my friend! We did not make it among the startups selected for a partnership with that company, sha. Maybe it is for another time (casual)
note: sha here at the end of the sentence, in its soft, sad tone (see k10)

text: Tunapenda kutoa shukrani zetu za dhati kwa uongozi wa ofisi kwa ushirikiano mzuri na huduma bora mlizotupatia.
label: positive
gloss: We would like to express our sincere gratitude to the office management for the good cooperation and excellent service provided to us (formal)
note: native-speaker revision of the author's draft 'Habari za asubuhi. Nataka kusema asante sana kwa ofisi yenu kwa kunisaidia vizuri na kazi yangu wiki hii.', which the author doubted was formal enough for professional correspondence

text: Asanteni sana washkaji zangu kwa usaidizi wenu jana, kwa kweli mmenisaidia pakubwa!
label: positive
gloss: Thanks a lot my friends for your help yesterday, you really helped me out big time! (casual)
note: washkaji is street vocabulary for close friends (native speakers' note); revision of the author's draft 'Asanteni sana jamani kwa kunisaidia jana! Nilikuwa na shida kubwa lakini nyinyi ni marafiki wa kweli kabisa.', where jamani is an expressive particle used to address friends affectionately

text: Tungependa kuwataarifu wateja wote kuwa ofisi zetu zitafungwa mapema leo kutokana na ukaguzi wa ndani.
label: neutral
gloss: We would like to inform all clients that our offices will close early today due to an internal inspection (formal)
note: revision of the author's draft 'Tunapenda kutoa taarifa kwamba ofisi yetu itafungwa mapema leo saa nane mchana kwa sababu ya mkutano wa wafanyakazi.' (closing at 2 PM for a staff meeting)

text: Wadau, kuwajulisha tu kwamba ofisi zetu zinafungwa mapema leo kwa ajili ya ukaguzi wa ndani.
label: neutral
gloss: Guys, just letting you know that our offices are closing early today for an internal inspection (casual)
note: wadau is used here loosely for group members, colleagues or clients in ordinary online chat (native speakers' note); revision of the author's draft 'Mambo jamani, nilitaka tu kuwaambia kwamba ofisi yetu inafungwa mapema leo kwa sababu kuna ukaguzi wa ndani.', where the author wondered whether a quick chat would say ukaguzi wa ndani or just ukaguzi

text: Tafadhali naomba msaada wa kupatiwa nakala ya taarifa ya fedha ya robo ya kwanza ya mwaka ili niweze kuikagua.
label: neutral
gloss: Please assist me with obtaining a copy of the first-quarter financial statement of the year so that I may review it (formal)
note: revision of the author's draft 'Heshima zenu. Tafadhali naomba unitumie ile ripoti ya mwisho wa mwezi kwenye barua pepe yangu ninapongojea.' (the end-of-month report by email), whose opening Heshima zenu the author doubted

text: Niaje rafiki, naomba uniazime chaja yako ya simu kwa muda mfupi kama hauitumii tafadhali?
label: neutral
gloss: Hey friend, could you lend me your phone charger for a short while if you're not using it, please? (casual)
note: Niaje is a common informal greeting (street Swahili, Sheng), like vipi or mambo (native speakers' note); revision of the author's draft 'Mambo! Samahani, naomba uniazime chaja yako ya simu kwa dakika chache tu? Betri yangu inakaribia kuzima kabisa.'

text: Ninawasilisha malalamiko haya kuhusu ucheleweshaji wa huduma niliyoomba majuma mawili yaliyopita bila kupewa taarifa yoyote.
label: negative
gloss: I am submitting this complaint regarding the delay of the service I requested two weeks ago without being given any explanation (formal)
note: revision of the author's draft 'Ninaandika kueleza kusikitishwa kwangu kwa sababu sikupewa huduma niliyoomba tangu wiki mbili, na hakuna aliyenijibu.', where the author doubted kusikitishwa kwangu as a calque of 'my disappointment'

text: Yaani siamini jinsi nilivyohudumiwa vibaya kule dukani leo, yule muhudumu alinijibu kwa dharau tupu bila sababu.
label: negative
gloss: I honestly can't believe how badly I was treated at the shop today, the attendant answered me with pure disrespect for no reason (casual)
note: revision of the author's draft 'Jamani, yule mwenye duka leo alinionyesha dharau mbaya sana bila sababu. Nilishangaa sana na nikakasirika kweli.'

text: si uko atankunda rwose, ahubwo ubushobozi bwamubanye bukeya
label: positive
gloss: It is not that s/he does not love me, for sure; rather, the means were not enough for him/her
note: a double negation, si uko atankunda, 'it is not that s/he does not love me', lands on 'he loves me'; ahubwo then gives the reason that stood in the way of the good experience, insufficient means; by the e501 rule the first judgment carries the speaker's weight and the next clause only explains

text: ntako atagize.
label: positive
gloss: there is nothing s/he did not do, s/he did all s/he could
note: idiomatic double negation, nta-ko a-ta-gize, literally 'there is no way s/he did not do'; the markers are nta and -ta-; said as praise of the effort, and also as consolation after a failure, where the effort is still praised

text: Ntimumuvuge nabi, si umuntu mubi na mba
label: positive
gloss: Do not speak ill of him/her, s/he is not a bad person at all
note: two negated negative words pointing the same way: nti- in ntimumuvuge nabi, 'do not speak badly of him/her', and si in si umuntu mubi, 'is not a bad person'; na mba is 'at all'

text: si bibi kutagira ubunebwe
label: positive
gloss: It is not bad not to be lazy
note: two negations, each on a negative word: si bibi 'it is not bad' and kutagira ubunebwe 'not to have laziness'; the surface holds only negative words and the meaning is positive

text: Muzi ko nta buntu bariya bantu bagira?
label: negative
gloss: Did you know that those people have no generosity?
note: nta, 'there is no', negates ubuntu 'generosity' (kugira ubuntu, 'to be generous'; not ubumuntu, 'humanity'); a rhetorical question

text: Aba bana ntibatojwe ikinyabupfura
label: negative
gloss: These kids were not raised with good manners
note: nti- negates gutozwa ikinyabupfura, 'to be trained in good manners'; the negated word is the good thing

text: Aya mafaranga ntabahagije ko muri gusaba andi?
label: negative
gloss: Isn't this money enough for you, that you are asking for more?
note: nta- in ntabahagije negates guhagira 'to be enough'; a rhetorical question that reproaches

text: Ntabwo iyi nzira ari nyabagendwa
label: negative
gloss: This road is not passable
note: ntabwo ... ari negates nyabagendwa, 'passable, fit to be walked on'; a plain statement about a thing

text: Ntibyemewe kujyana impamagarakure ku ishuri ku banyeshuri bose bari munsi y'imyaka cumi n'umunani
label: neutral
gloss: It is not allowed to bring phones to school for students under the age of eighteen
note: nti- negates kwemerwa 'to be allowed'; a rule, no feeling in it

text: Ntabwo muri burenge aha nimuterekana ibyangombwa byanyu
label: neutral
gloss: You will not go past here if you do not show your ID papers
note: two negations in one rule: ntabwo ... burenge 'you will not pass' and nimuterekana 'if you do not show'; said by a gatekeeper, a condition rather than a feeling

text: Ntabwo amatwi n'amaso biba ku gihimba cy'umubiri
label: neutral
gloss: Ears and eyes are not on the trunk of the body
note: ntabwo negates biba, 'are (located)'; a plain fact of anatomy, no feeling

text: Ntabwo amata arishwa inyama mu muco Nyarwanda
label: neutral
gloss: In Rwandan culture, milk is not taken together with meat in one meal
note: ntabwo negates arishwa, 'is taken together with'; a cultural fact, no feeling

text: ntabwo ari uko tudakunda abanyeshuri bacu
label: positive
gloss: it is not that we do not love our students
note: double negation, ntabwo ari uko ... tudakunda, with -da- in the verb; lands on 'we love our students', the opening of a defense

text: Mambo! Rafiki yangu hakukataa kununua chakula cha jioni.
label: positive
gloss: Hi! My friend did not refuse to buy dinner
note: author's draft, confirmed by the native readers; hakukataa negates kukataa 'to refuse'

text: Sijasahau kuleta kitabu chako leo.
label: positive
gloss: I have not forgotten to bring your book today
note: author's draft, the pronoun Mimi dropped on the native readers' advice as redundant; sijasahau negates kusahau 'to forget'

text: Hatuchukii kusoma lugha ya Kiswahili shuleni.
label: positive
gloss: We do not hate studying the Swahili language at school
note: author's draft, the pronoun Sisi dropped on the native readers' advice; they find 'we do not hate' an awkward phrasing in casual talk, kept on purpose since the negated kuchukia 'to hate' is the test

text: Habari, fundi haji kutengeneza kompyuta yangu sasa hivi.
label: neutral
gloss: Hello, the technician is not coming to fix my computer right now
note: author's draft, confirmed by the native readers; haji negates kuja 'to come'; a fact

text: Watoto hawasomi maktaba leo kwa sababu imefungwa.
label: neutral
gloss: The children are not studying at the library today because it is closed
note: author's draft, confirmed by the native readers; hawasomi negates kusoma 'to study'; a fact

text: Habari za asubuhi! Simu yangu mpya haifanyi kazi vizuri.
label: negative
gloss: Good morning! My new phone is not working well
note: author's draft, confirmed by the native readers; haifanyi kazi vizuri negates 'works well'

text: Kaka yangu hapendi kunywa chai yenye sukari nyingi.
label: neutral
gloss: My brother does not like to drink tea with a lot of sugar
note: author's draft, confirmed by the native readers; hapendi negates kupenda 'to like', yet the sentence states a third person's preference as a fact, with no feeling of the speaker in it; a trap for a model that reads every negated 'like' as negative

text: Hatutakuwa na furaha kama mvua itanyesha kesho.
label: negative
gloss: We will not be happy if it rains tomorrow
note: author's draft, the pronoun Sisi dropped on the native readers' advice; hatutakuwa na furaha negates kuwa na furaha 'to be happy'

text: Mwanangu, usiwe na wasiwasi, bosi hajafuta ile bonasi ya sikukuu.
label: positive
gloss: My friend, don't worry, the boss has not canceled that holiday bonus
note: native readers' sentence; hajafuta negates kufuta 'to cancel', and usiwe na wasiwasi 'don't worry' is a second negation pointing the same way; mwanangu, literally 'my child', is a common casual term of endearment among peers in Tanzania, like 'my brother'; bonasi 'bonus' carries a good feeling on its own

text: Mshikaji wangu hakukataa kunisaidia wakati sikuwa na nauli.
label: positive
gloss: My buddy did not refuse to help me when I had no fare
note: native readers' sentence; hakukataa negates kukataa 'to refuse'; mshikaji is a close friend or buddy in urban Tanzanian chat; kunisaidia 'to help me' is a good word on its own, and sikuwa na nauli 'I had no fare' a second negation stating a fact

text: Hatujajuta kuhamia kwenye ofisi hii mpya hata kidogo.
label: positive
gloss: We have not regretted moving to this new office at all
note: native readers' sentence; hatujajuta negates kujuta 'to regret'; hata kidogo 'at all' strengthens the negation

text: Leo jioni gari langu haliwaki kabisa, itabidi nishuke kwa miguu.
label: negative
gloss: This evening my car is not starting at all, I will have to walk
note: native readers' sentence, offered as neutral; haliwaki negates kuwaka 'to start (an engine)'; kwa miguu 'on foot'; labeled negative by the author, since a car that will not start and a walk home are a complaint

text: Kesho hatutaenda kazini kwa sababu ni siku ya mapumziko.
label: neutral
gloss: Tomorrow we will not go to work because it is a day off
note: native readers' sentence; hatutaenda negates kwenda 'to go'; siku ya mapumziko 'rest day' is the relaxed word for a day off, where siku kuu or likizo would be formal

text: Kiukweli, jua la leo halipendezi kabisa, linachoma sana.
label: negative
gloss: Honestly, today's sun is not pleasant at all, it is burning hot
note: native readers' sentence; halipendezi negates kupendeza 'to be pleasant'; kiukweli opens a casual opinion; linachoma sana 'it burns a lot' is a second negative clue, so this item does not test the negation alone

text: Chakula cha mgahawa ule hakivutii hata kidogo siku hizi.
label: negative
gloss: The food at that restaurant is not appealing at all these days
note: native readers' sentence; hakivutii negates kuvutia 'to be appealing'; hata kidogo 'at all'; siku hizi 'these days'

text: Sherehe ya leo haijafana vile tulivyotegemea.
label: negative
gloss: Today's party has not been as lively as we expected
note: native readers' sentence; haijafana negates kufana, the verb for a party or an event that is lively and successful

text: Uyu mwana afite uburere rwose
label: positive
gloss: This child has been well raised indeed
note: affirmative control for the negation pair

text: Uyu mwana nta burere afite rwose
label: negative
gloss: This child has not been well raised at all
note: row k26 negated with detached nta; same intensifier, flipped meaning

text: Uyu mwana ntaburere afite rwose
label: negative
gloss: This child has not been well raised at all
note: k27 with nta attached to the noun, the common typed form

text: Uyu musore nta mutima mubi agira
label: positive
gloss: This gentleman is not unkind
note: negation of a bad quality; contains mubi and nta yet the meaning is positive

text: Ni ukuri bazaguhe igihembo cy'umuntu ugira ubugugu kurusha abandi
label: negative
gloss: For real, may you be given the award of the person ranked top in selfishness among all
note: praise frame (an award) with an insulting content; positive words, negative intent

text: Nuko ye, nawe ngo uri za bagabo ye!
label: negative
gloss: Of course, we can see, and you are said to be a so-called man!
note: ngo frames a claim the speaker rejects: 'so-called man'; mockery of a man failing his role

text: Aka kanya uhise usezera akazi se 😂 ?
label: negative
gloss: And right away, you have just quit the job 😂?
note: laughing emoji as mockery of someone who quit a job almost at once

text: Mwa bantu mwe! Uriya mubyeyi ni umugome. Ukuntu agira abana b'abagiraneza se!
label: negative
gloss: Oh people! That parent is cruel. And how come s/he has such kind children!
note: two opposite judgments, no contrast word; in Kinyarwanda the first judgment carries the speaker's weight

text: Mwa bantu mwe! Bariya bana ni abagiraneza. Ukuntu bafite umubyeyi w'umugome.
label: positive
gloss: Oh people! Those children are so kind. And how come they have such a cruel parent!
note: mirror of the previous item: kind children first, cruel parent second; the first judgment carries the weight

text: Muri kiriya kigo ngo bahemba neza, ariko ngo baragukoresha nawe ukabyumva koko
label: negative
gloss: In that organization they pay good money, but it is said that they make you work for it and you really feel it
note: positive first, ariko then negative: after ariko the negative clause becomes a warning and carries the weight

text: Muri kiriya kigo ngo baragukoresha nawe ukabyumva koko, ariko ngo banahemba neza
label: positive
gloss: In that organization it is said that they make you work and you really feel it, but they also pay good money
note: mirror: negative first, ariko then positive; the positive clause reassures and carries the weight (disi would mark the sympathy)

text: ndebera vraiment! 😢
label: negative
gloss: Look at this, for real! 😢
note: French vraiment inside Kinyarwanda, a half translation of ni ukuri; the shock is carried by the emoji

text: Et d'ailleurs uze hano nkubwire
label: neutral
gloss: And besides, come here and let me tell you
note: French discourse marker et d'ailleurs, a colonial-era borrowing with no Kinyarwanda equivalent; the rest is a summons

text: courage nshuti yanjye. Turagushyigikiye pe
label: positive
gloss: Courage, my friend. We stand behind you, truly
note: French courage carries the support, no exact Kinyarwanda word for it; pe is an intensifier like rwose

text: Bagenzi bahire, turabamenyesha ko indege igeze neza ku kibuga mpuzamahanga cya Kigali, i Kanombe. Mwakoze guhitamo Rwandair, murakaza neza i Kigali
label: positive
gloss: Dear passengers, we inform you that the plane has landed safely at Kigali International Airport, Kanombe. Thank you for choosing RwandAir, welcome to Kigali (formal)
note: landing announcement: formal thanks and welcome; neza twice and mwakoze in an official register

text: Mu rwego rwo gukumira ikwirakwira ry'icyorezo cya Covid 19, gahunda ya "Guma mu rugo" irakomeje
label: negative
gloss: In order to prevent the spread of the Covid 19 epidemic, the Stay at Home program continues (formal)
note: official notice that the lockdown continues: bad news in a neutral register, no sentiment word

text: Gukoresha ubwiherero ntibyemewe
label: neutral
gloss: Using the toilet is not allowed (formal)
note: cabin announcement; the prohibition nti- is procedural, not a sentiment
